NUZZLE.scope: The five units in appliesTo declare NUZZLE in this production reference. The strategy is shared; the unit-specific differences are only the star count (table index), the passive and the stats. Pachirisu's own passive (Passive.PACHIRISU) is NOT covered here (see passiveGaps).
NUZZLE.summary: Jumps to a free cell next to the enemy that is farthest from the caster, retargets it, then paralyses it and deals special damage. If no free cell exists anywhere near, the caster stays and hits its current target.

targeting.who: the farthest targettable enemy that has a free adjacent cell (ties: first found in board scan order); the cast target is replaced by it
targeting.note: if board.getFarthestTargetCoordinateAvailablePlace returns null, the original cast target is hit and the caster does not move

geometry.shape: single target; caster relocates to a free cell adjacent to it (selected as the free adjacent cell farthest from the caster)

effects.scaling: AP: damage x (1 + AP/100) (apBoost true is passed); the cast's crit flag multiplies by critPower only if the cast crit (needs ABILITY_CRIT: canCritByDefault is false)
effects.resolution: then the target's SPE_DEF division (damage / (1 + 0.05 x SPE_DEF), ceil, min 1) and later untraced modifiers; blocked entirely by protect / skydiving / magicBounce

statusEffects.scaling: none from AP (triggerParalysis apBoost defaults to false and is not passed); not crit-scaled
statusEffects.applicationOrder: paralysis is applied BEFORE the damage call in the source
statusEffects.guards: not applied if runeProtect or IMMUNITY_PARALYSIS; storm weather x1.3 (Electric Quartz lowers it); aquatic/Odd Keystone reductions via applyStatusDurationReductions; a new paralysis only replaces the remaining time if it is longer
statusEffects.combatEffect: while paralysed the target's speed counts as half in the attack interval and in move speed, and it cannot dodge basic attacks. Uses of paralysis found in attacking-state.ts, move-speed.ts, pokemon-state.ts and pokemon-entity.ts are these three; other files were not searched.

starBehavior.note: indexed by the casting entity's stars; the 4-star column (200 damage, 6000 ms) is not reachable by any of the five units' bare factory star counts (stars are 1, 2, 3, 3, 3). Whether other mechanics raise an entity's star count was not examined.

NUZZLE.positionalConditions: Needs at least one targettable enemy to select a destination. The caster moves to a free cell adjacent to the farthest enemy; if that enemy has no free adjacent cell, the code keeps an earlier (nearer) candidate if one was found, otherwise falls back to the free cell closest to the farthest enemy; if nothing is free, no move and the original target is hit.
NUZZLE.repeatedCastsAndModes: No stored state: each cast re-selects the farthest enemy, jumps, paralyses and hits. No modes. Two casts on the same target extend paralysis only if the new duration exceeds the remaining one.
NUZZLE.rawVsResolved: Declared raw: damage 25/50/100 (1/2/3 stars) and paralysis 3000 ms for 1-3 stars. The damage dealt is the raw value x (1 + AP/100), then SPE_DEF division (ceil, at least 1) and untraced modifiers; the paralysis length is the raw value after the listed status modifiers.

DRAGON_RAGE.scope: Gyarados only (the single catalog unit with this skill). DRAGON_RAGE is used by no other registry entry and the effect flag EffectEnum.DRAGON_RAGE appears only in dragon-rage.ts in the server code (grep over app/*.ts; client animation files excluded).
DRAGON_RAGE.summary: Gives the caster an initial shield and starts a 6-pulse effect: each pulse (every 1000 timer units) adds more shield and hits all adjacent enemies with special damage; when the effect ends, the shield it granted is partly converted into healing (40 %).

targeting.who: no target needed (castable anywhere); pulses hit adjacent enemies of the caster

geometry.shape: the 8 cells adjacent to the caster's current position, re-read at each pulse (the caster may have moved)

effects.condition: each pulse, to every enemy on an adjacent cell
effects.scaling: AP: x(1 + AP/100) (no apBoost argument => handleSpecialDamage default true); crit only if the cast itself crit (needs ABILITY_CRIT), and that crit flag is stored in the effect at creation
effects.resolution: then SPE_DEF division per pulse, ceil, min 1, and later modifiers

effects.condition: once on the first cast (initial) and once per pulse
effects.scaling: addShield(value, caster, apBoost 1, crit): x(1 + AP/100), x critPower if the cast crit, halved if the unit is enraged, rounded; Big Eater Belt hook in PokemonEntity.addShield
effects.resolution: the amount actually received can exceed (AP) or fall below (enrage) the raw value, while the stored counter `shieldGiven` adds the RAW value only

effects.condition: when the effect ends (7th timer fire) or when the ability is cast again while active

declaredRaw.note: shieldGiven = raw initial shield + raw per-pulse shields added so far; the same amount is removed from the caster's shield

perUnitRaw.GYARADOS: round(0.4 x min(shield, 135)) at most, i.e. 54, when the cast ran its full course

effects.scaling: none from AP or crit (handleHeal called with apBoost 0, crit false); wound => 0, burn and enrage halve, zenith weather x1.2, rounded, capped at missing HP
effects.resolution: depends on how much of the granted shield is still on the unit; a conversion removes shield, so it is an exchange, not an extra shield

starBehavior.note: indexed by the casting entity's stars: Gyarados (3 stars) uses initial 45, per-pulse shield 15, per-pulse damage 15. The 1/2/4-star columns are listed as the table's content only.

DRAGON_RAGE.positionalConditions: None for casting. Damage depends on which enemies are on the 8 adjacent cells at each pulse.
DRAGON_RAGE.repeatedCastsAndModes: State: a DragonRageEffect with ticksRemaining (6) and shieldGiven. FIRST cast: adds the initial shield and creates the effect. CAST WHILE ACTIVE: no new initial shield is added; the active effect converts its tracked shield into healing right away (consumeShield) and ticksRemaining is reset to 6 (the effect's 1000-unit timer is not reset). The effect ends on the pulse where ticksRemaining would go below 0, i.e. after 6 damaging pulses the 7th timer fire ends it and converts what is left. Each cast still spends maxPP of PP.
DRAGON_RAGE.rawVsResolved: Declared raw for 3 stars: initial shield 45, per pulse shield 15 and damage 15, 6 pulses; tracked raw shield total 45 + 6 x 15 = 135; heal at most round(0.4 x 135) = 54 when the whole tracked amount is still on the unit. Actual shield includes AP scaling and may be lower after damage; the heal is capped by missing HP and reduced by burn/enrage/wound.

THRASH.scope: Mankey, Primeape and Annihilape (all declare THRASH in this production reference). The strategy is shared; stars select the attack multiplier, and baseAtk is read from the entity, so a Primeape's value depends on its permanent attack. Primeape's passive PRIMEAPE is a separate record (passives.PRIMEAPE).
THRASH.summary: Self-buff: adds attack equal to a star-dependent percentage of the unit's base attack, then confuses the caster itself for 3000 ms (not refreshed while already confused). No enemy is targeted and no damage is dealt by the cast.

targeting.who: the caster only; no target needed

effects.scaling: addAttack(value, caster, apBoost 1, crit): value x (1 + AP/100) x (critPower if the cast crit), rounded, then Big Eater / Twist Band hooks (Twist Band is a no-op for a positive self buff); ATK floor 1
effects.resolution: baseAtk is the entity's ATK at creation (the board Pokemon's atk, which includes earlier permanent attack); the buff is NOT permanent (permanent defaults to false) and has no expiry timer in the ability code, so it lasts for the fight

statusEffects.scaling: none (triggerConfusion apBoost defaults to false and is not passed)
statusEffects.guards: not applied if the unit is already confused (so a recast during confusion does NOT extend it), runeProtect, or IMMUNITY_CONFUSION (e.g. after Persim Berry); sandstorm x1.3; reductions through applyStatusDurationReductions; a Persim Berry holder eats it
statusEffects.combatEffect: while confused, every basic-attack target selection is replaced: with a 50 % (luck-adjusted) roll the unit keeps normal enemy targeting among the nearest in range+1, otherwise allies are also eligible, the nearest is picked and the unit itself is added as a candidate; when confusion ends the target is cleared. This code is in the attacking state; the moving state has no confusion branch in the lines searched. Ability casting does not need a target for THRASH.

starBehavior.note: 1 and 2 stars share 100 %; 3 stars is 120 %; the 150 % entry is unreachable by these three units' bare star counts. Absolute values depend on baseAtk: 7 / 20 / 30 on the bare catalog instances.

THRASH.positionalConditions: None. The cast has no range or target requirement; the self-confusion affects who the unit attacks afterwards.
THRASH.repeatedCastsAndModes: Each cast adds another ATK increment computed from the same baseAtk (the increments stack within the fight, with no cap in the ability). The confusion is only (re)applied when the unit is not confused, so casts closer together than 3000 ms (plus any lengthening) do not extend it. No modes.
THRASH.rawVsResolved: Declared raw: attack + floor(percent/100 x baseAtk), then x(1 + AP/100) and rounding; Mankey +7 and Primeape +20 (bare baseAtk), Annihilape +36 (120 % of 30). Confusion 3000 ms before duration modifiers.

SURGE_SURFER.nameCollision: Passive.SURGE_SURFER (this record) is NOT EffectEnum.SURGE_SURFER, the aquatic-synergy tier effect that cuts status durations (x0.3) in applyStatusDurationReductions. The two share a name only.
SURGE_SURFER.kind: stat-while-field passive (no PassiveEffects entry: logic lives in Status.add/remove*Field)
SURGE_SURFER.summary: Each time the holder gains an electric field or a psychic field (through the Status add-field methods) it gets +30 speed; losing that field removes the 30 again. Both fields: +60. Nothing else is done by the passive itself.
SURGE_SURFER.trigger: Status.addElectricField / Status.addPsychicField called on the holder while the field flag was false; Status.removeElectricField / removePsychicField while it was true

effects.scaling: addSpeed(30, self, apBoost 0, crit false): no AP or crit scaling; Big Eater Belt/Twist Band hooks still run in addSpeed; speed is clamped at 0..MAX_SPEED

conditions: The add method returns early if that field flag is already true, so each field gives +30 at most once (max +60 with both).
The holder is recognised by entity.passive === Passive.SURGE_SURFER; entity.passive is set in the PokemonEntity constructor through changePassive (no effect registered there).

Field sources that go through addElectricField / addPsychicField: ELECTRIC_TERRAIN and PSYCHIC_TERRAIN synergy effects (the unit must have that type: Alolan Raichu has both Electric and Psychic types), units flagged supercharged at simulation start, a storm-weather lightning strike on an Electric-type unit, Terrain Extender (item), Herba Mystica Spicy/Sour dishes, Terrain Pulse, Electrify, Expanding Force.

Field sources that set the flag DIRECTLY (Volt Surge, Tadbulb-supercharge passive, Pincurchin passive) bypass the add method, so they give a field flag but NOT the +30 speed (and a later remove call would then subtract 30 that was never added: unexamined).

Terrain Extender selects the first of the holder's types (in its type order) among Electric/Grass/Psychic/Fairy: for Alolan Raichu (Electric, Fairy, Psychic) that is Electric, so the item alone gives the electric field only.
SURGE_SURFER.relatedFieldEffects: Independent of this passive, an attacker with an electric field deals x1.2 damage in handleDamage and a psychic field a second x1.2 (the multipliers stack). That is a field effect, not part of SURGE_SURFER.
SURGE_SURFER.resetBehaviour: Entity status is built per fight; there is no persisted state. Within a fight the speed is removed when the field is removed (death of an ELECTRIC_TERRAIN / PSYCHIC_TERRAIN passive unit removes the field from its team). No timer or stack counter exists.

PRIMEAPE.notApplied: Mankey and Annihilape declare passive NONE in the catalog: the passive and its stacking apply only to Primeape.
PRIMEAPE.summary: Every time the Primeape entity dies or starts a resurrection, it gains +1 ATK (permanent: also written to the board unit) and +1 stack; its STACK evolution rule needs 10 stacks and evolves it into Annihilape mid-fight.

triggers.note: applied on KO and does not proc when the unit resurrects instead (effect.ts comment); death path runs PokemonEntity.onDeath from triggerDeath
run in the resurrection branch of handleDamage when status.resurrection is set and hp <= 0

effects.scaling: addAttack(1, self, apBoost 0, crit false, permanent true): no AP/crit scaling; Big Eater Belt (x1.25 rounded down) leaves 1 unchanged; ATK floor 1; the permanent flag also updates the board Pokemon unless the entity is a ghost opponent
addStack(): returns immediately when the entity has no player (e.g. a non-player opponent), otherwise increments the board unit's stacks and mirrors them to the entity

evolution.declared: Primeape: evolution ANNIHILAPE, evolutionRule STACK, stacksRequired 10 (Mankey declares evolution PRIMEAPE and no rule of its own, so it uses the inherited default rule, not examined here; Annihilape declares no evolution)
evolution.trigger: PokemonEntity.addStack calls EvolutionManager.tryEvolve ONLY when stacks === stacksRequired (exact equality) and the rule type is STACK
evolution.gate: StackEvolutionHandler.canEvolve: false when holding Eviolite or not on the player's board; otherwise stacks >= stacksRequired
evolution.result: player.transformPokemon builds the evolved unit, carries permanent stat deltas (atk delta versus a fresh Primeape is re-applied), re-adds items, then Annihilape.onAcquired subtracts 10 attack (30 - 20) 'to revert permanent atk buff stacked for evolution'
evolution.plainCaseArithmetic: Primeape atk 20 + 10 permanent points = 30 at the 10th stack; Annihilape factory 30 + carried delta 10 - onAcquired 10 = 30. This assumes exactly 10 permanent points and no other permanent atk changes; it is arithmetic on the cited lines, not an observed result
evolution.checkedAgainstOldNotes: The earlier pilot-evolution note was re-checked against the source: STACK rule, stacksRequired 10, the === test, the >= handler, the Eviolite/board gates and the +1 atk/addStack pair all hold. Newly established here: death/resurrection are mutually exclusive triggers, addStack ignores entities without a player, the atk delta is carried through carryOverPermanentStats and trimmed by Annihilape.onAcquired.

conditions: Eviolite blocks evolution at the moment the 10th stack lands; because addStack tests equality, stacks 11 and beyond never call tryEvolve again, so a Primeape that reached 10 stacks while holding Eviolite does not evolve from later deaths in this code path (inference from the === test; other tryEvolve callers not exhaustively listed).
canEvolve also requires the unit to be on the player's board (stack-evolution-handler.ts:9).
A resurrection and the death that follows it each give a stack when they occur (two events), but a single hit that resurrects gives one (the death effect does not proc then).
PRIMEAPE.resetBehaviour: The stack count lives on the board Pokemon (refToBoardPokemon.stacks) and the permanent attack on its atk, so both persist across fights in the code read. No reset of stacks to 0 for Primeape was found (pattern search over `stacks = ` assignments in app/; not an exhaustive proof). The entity copy of stacks is taken from the board unit at fight start.
